prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a construction site from an elevated viewpoint where the camera wearer pans left across five frames: Frame 1 faces a wall ~1–1.5 m away with a vertical wooden pole (~0.5 m, within the wearer's arm's reach) and a white pipe (~1 m) in front of it, while Frames 2–5 reveal an open ground area below and to the left containing sacks, buckets, and pans at ~1.5–4 m. Two workers stand on the lower ground about 0.8–1 m apart: a nearer person in a pink shirt (~2–2.5 m from the wearer, facing right toward the wall and away from the camera) partially occluded behind the foreground wooden pole and hanging ropes (~0.5–0.8 m, within the wearer's arm's reach), and a farther person in a plaid shirt behind and to the left (~3–3.5 m away, turning from facing right in Frame 2 to facing and looking toward the camera wearer in Frames 3–5). A bucket, pans, and a wooden pole on the ground lie within arm's reach of the two workers, while the foreground pole and hanging ropes remain within arm's reach of the camera wearer across all frames. This map clarifies the continuous distance gradient along the right-hand wall, the ground plane, and the foreground separation of the hanging ropes and pole from the workers below, which is harder to judge in the cluttered RGB image. However, the depth map is unreliable inside the hanging rope loops—where background wall pixels bleed through with bright foreground depth—and in the upper-left background of Frames 2–5, where walls and rubble collapse into uniform black saturation.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities in Frames 2–5 after detecting nothing in Frame 1, locating the two standing workers (~2–2.5 m and ~3–3.5 m from the camera wearer, ~0.8–1 m apart) and a single metal pan labeled as a 'bowl' on the ground to their left (~3.5 m away) in Frames 3–5. Relative to the camera wearer, the plaid-shirted worker is positioned behind and slightly left of the pink-shirted worker, with the detected bowl below and to the left of both workers' feet and just beyond their immediate arm's reach, while closer buckets and sacks within their reach go unlabeled. Across Frames 2–5, as the camera pans left and stabilizes, the masks show the pink-shirted worker leaning forward toward the right-hand wall in Frame 5 while the plaid-shirted worker stays upright and turns his torso and head toward the camera wearer. The map provides sharp silhouette boundaries separating the two adjacent workers from the similarly toned dirt, sacks, and plastered wall in Frames 3–5. However, it is unreliable in Frame 2 where the foreground wooden pole and ropes split the pink-shirted worker into multiple overlapping 'person' masks that erroneously include the pole and rope, it swaps the instance colours between the two workers in Frame 5, and it fails to segment the pipes, poles, sacks, buckets, and other pans.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a 2D yellow body skeleton for only one worker per frame from Frame 2 to Frame 5, completely omitting the camera wearer and all scene objects. In Frame 2, it tracks the farther plaid-shirted worker (~3–3.5 m away on the left) facing right with his right arm extended downward toward thepink-shirted worker (~0.8–1 m in front of him), whereas in Frames 3–5 it switches to tracking only the nearer pink-shirted worker (~2–2.5 m away on the right). In Frames 3–5, the tracked pink-shirted worker stands in profile facing right toward the wall and away from the camera wearer, with his torso leaning progressively forward in Frame 5 and his right arm hanging down within arm's reach of the wooden pole and wall in front of him. This skeletal representation makes the worker's profile orientation, shoulder-to-hip alignment, forward lean in Frame 5, and leg placement behind the occluding foreground pole immediately apparent despite heavy visual clutter in the RGB frames. However, the map is unreliable because it misses the pink-shirted worker in Frame 2, completely drops the plaid-shirted worker in Frames 3–5 even though he stands clearly visible and looking toward the camera, and detects no magenta hand skeletons in any frame.
